column5: He is studying advanced Chinese.
column6: 高级 means "high-level": 高级班 (an advanced class), 高级饭馆 (a high-class restaurant), 高级经理 (a senior manager).

column4: 这家公司做高科技产品。
column5: This company makes high-tech products.
column6: 高科技 is high technology. It often comes before a noun: 高科技产品, 高科技公司.

column5: He works very efficiently.
column6: 高效 means getting a lot done in a short time. It comes before a noun (高效的方法) or after 很 (很高效).

column3: to do; to be up to (casual)
column5: What are you up to?
column6: 搞 is a casual all-purpose verb for "do", "make" or "deal with": 搞错 (to get wrong), 搞清楚 (to get clear), 搞好 (to do well).

column5: He says goodbye to his friend at the station.
column6: 告别 is a more formal way to say goodbye: 告别家人 (to say goodbye to the family).

column5: The lyrics of this song are very beautiful.
column6: 歌词 are the words of a song. 词 means "words".

column5: He is very good at singing Chinese songs.
column6: 歌曲 is a formal word for a song. In speech people say 歌 or 一首歌.

column3: to be separated by; to be apart
column4: 我家和学校隔着一条河。
column5: My home and the school are separated by a river.
column6: 隔 is to be apart in space or time: 隔着河 (across a river), 隔一天 (every other day).

column5: The air after the rain is especially fresh.
column6: 格外 means "more than usual". It comes before an adjective: 格外高兴.

column5: A few individual students did not come to class.
column6: 个别 means "one or two, very few": 个别人 (a few individuals). It is not "every".

column3: all walks of life; every trade
column4: 各行各业的人都来参加了。
column5: People from all walks of life came to take part.
column6: 各行各业 means every profession and trade. 行 is read háng here, meaning a trade or line of work.

column5: This is my personal view.
column6: 个人 is one person as opposed to a group, or "personal": 个人的想法. It is different from 两个人, where 个 is a measure word.

column5: She has a strong personality.
column6: 个性 is the special character of a person: 个性很强 (strong-minded), 很有个性 (full of personality).

column4: 下课以后，大家各自回家。
column5: After class, everyone goes home on their own.
column6: 各自 comes before the verb and shows that each person acts separately: 各自回家.

column3: root; measure word for long thin things
column5: The roots of this tree are very long.
column6: 根 is a root (树根). As a measure word it counts long thin things: 一根筷子, 一根线.

column5: He does not know about this at all.
column6: 根本 with a negative means "not at all": 根本不, 根本没. It is also a noun and adjective for the root or basic part (根本问题 = a fundamental problem).

column4: 这个旧电池需要更换了。
column5: This old battery needs replacing now.
column6: 更换 is to swap something for a new one: 更换电池, 更换衣服. 更 is read gēng here, not gèng.

column5: This software is often updated.
column6: 更新 is to replace the old with the new: 更新软件 (to update software). 更 is read gēng here.

column5: The exam results will be announced tomorrow.
column6: 公布 is to make something known to everyone in an official way: 公布成绩 (to announce results).

column5: This project will take two years.
column6: 工程 is a big building or technical project, such as a bridge or a road.

column5: He is an engineer.
column6: 工程师 is a trained engineer. 师 is a skilled person, as in 老师.

column5: He has many tools for repairing cars.
column6: 工具 is a tool for a job. It is also used for any means: 交通工具 (a means of transport).

column5: This phone has many functions.
column6: 功能 is what a machine or a thing can do: 新功能 (a new feature).

column4: 老师对每个学生都很公平。
column5: The teacher is fair to every student.
column6: 公平 means treating everyone equally. Its opposite is 不公平.

column4: 他在政府工作，是公务员。
column5: He works for the government and is a civil servant.
column6: 公务员 is a person who works for the government.

column5: Congratulations, you have got into university!
column6: 恭喜 is said to congratulate someone: 恭喜你, 恭喜你们. Add the reason after it: 恭喜你毕业. 恭喜 is more spoken and warmer than 祝贺, which is a little formal.

column4: 这个城市的工业很发达。
column5: The industry of this city is very developed.
column6: 工业 is factory industry. 产业 is a whole branch of the economy.

column5: The workmanship of this chair is very good.
column6: 工艺 is the skill of making things, often by hand: 传统工艺 (traditional craft).

column4: 他住在城里的一套小公寓。
column5: He lives in a small flat in the city.
column6: 公寓 is an apartment building or a flat in one.

column4: 他为学校做出了很大的贡献。
column5: He has made a great contribution to the school.
column6: 贡献 is a verb and a noun. 做出贡献 means "to make a contribution".

column4: 我们和邻居共享一个花园。
column5: We share a garden with our neighbours.
column6: 共享 is to use or enjoy something together: 共享单车 (a shared bike).

column5: Good friends should communicate more.
column6: 沟通 is to talk so that people understand each other: 和父母沟通 (to communicate with parents).

column3: to form; to make up (what it consists of)
column4: 这个句子由五个词构成。
column5: This sentence is made up of five words.
column6: 构成 is to form or make up: 由……构成 means "to be made up of".

column5: This city has many ancient trees.
column6: 古 means ancient. It is mostly used inside words: 古代, 古老, 古书, 古人.

column4: 孩子们在学校里学打鼓。
column5: The children learn to play drums at school.
column6: 鼓 is a drum. 打鼓 is to play the drum. As a verb it also means to bulge.

column5: People in ancient times wrote with brushes.
column6: 古代 is ancient times, long ago. Its opposite is 现代 (modern times).

column5: This is an ancient city.
column6: 古老 describes something with a very long history: 古老的文化 (an ancient culture).

column5: Everyone applauds him.
column6: 鼓掌 is a verb plus object, so it splits: 鼓了掌.

column4: 他每天在固定的时间锻炼。
column5: He exercises at a fixed time every day.
column6: 固定 is a verb ("to fix in place") and an adjective ("fixed, regular"): 固定的时间, 固定电话 (a landline).

column5: I miss my hometown very much.
column6: 故乡 is the place where you were born and grew up, said in a warm, written way. 家乡 is the everyday word.

column5: You must register first before seeing a doctor.
column6: 挂号 is to register at a hospital to see a doctor. It is a verb plus object: 挂了号, 挂号费 (the registration fee).

column5: This sound is very strange.
column6: 怪 means "strange" (很怪), "to blame" (别怪他) and, before an adjective in speech, "rather" (怪好看的).

column5: The shop closes at ten in the evening.
column6: 关闭 is a formal word for 关: 关闭商店, 关闭手机.

column4: 他每天观察天气的变化。
column5: He observes the changes in the weather every day.
column6: 观察 is to watch carefully to find something out.

column5: I do not agree with your point of view.
column6: 观点 is a person's way of seeing an issue: 我的观点 (my view).

column4: 老人的观念和年轻人不一样。
column5: Old people's ideas are different from young people's.
column6: 观念 is a settled way of thinking: 旧观念 (old ideas), 时间观念 (a sense of time).

column5: He is the champion of this competition.
column6: 冠军 is the winner. 得冠军 means "to win the championship".

column4: 欢迎您光临我们的饭馆。
column5: We welcome you to our restaurant.
column6: 光临 is a polite word for someone's visit, used by shops and restaurants: 欢迎光临 (welcome).

column5: His future is bright.
column6: 光明 is light, and also hope: 光明的未来 (a bright future).

column5: The light in this room is very good.
column6: 光线 is the light you can see in a place. 灯光 is the light from lamps.

column5: His range of knowledge is very wide.
column6: 广 means wide in range or extent: 兴趣广, 范围广. It is read guǎng.

column5: They are dancing in the square.
column6: 广场 is a large open public place in a city.

column4: 广大学生都喜欢这位老师。
column5: The broad body of students all like this teacher.
column6: 广大 describes a large area or a large number of people: 广大观众 (the broad audience).

column5: His interests are very wide-ranging.
column6: 广泛 means covering many fields: 兴趣广泛, 广泛使用 (widely used).

column5: His life is very regular.
column6: 规律 is a pattern in how things happen: 有规律 (regular), 生活规律 (a regular routine).

column5: The scale of this company is very big.
column6: 规模 is how big something is, such as a company or an event: 大规模 (large-scale).

column5: The game has many rules.
column6: 规则 is a rule: 比赛规则, 交通规则 (traffic rules).

column5: Excuse me, what is your surname?
column6: 贵姓 is a polite way to ask someone's surname. The answer is 我姓……

column5: The clothes are in the cupboard.
column6: 柜子 is a piece of furniture for keeping things.

column5: The ball rolled under the table.
column6: 滚 is to roll. In speech 滚! means "get lost", which is rude.

column5: There is hot water in the pot.
column6: 锅 is a cooking pot or wok. 火锅 is "hot pot".

column5: She likes to paint traditional Chinese paintings.
column6: 国画 is Chinese brush and ink painting, often of mountains, flowers and birds.

column5: We are going travelling on National Day.
column6: 国庆 is the National Day of China on 1 October. 国庆节 is the holiday, which lasts a week.

column4: 天气预报说会下雨，果然下雨了。
column5: The weather forecast said it would rain, and sure enough it rained.
column6: 果然 means the result is just what you expected.

column5: In autumn, there is a lot of fruit on the trees.
column6: 果实 is the fruit of a plant. It also means the result of work.

column5: Overwork is not good for the body.
column6: 过度 means too much: 过度使用 (overuse), 过度紧张 (too nervous).

column5: He has gone too far by doing this.
column6: 过分 means going beyond what is reasonable: 太过分了 (that is going too far).

column5: I am allergic to milk.
column6: 过敏 is a verb: 对……过敏 means "to be allergic to".

column3: to expire; to be out of date
column5: This milk has already expired.
column6: 过期 is to pass the date: 过期的药 (out-of-date medicine). It is a verb plus object.

column5: Do not worry too much.
column6: 过于 is a written "too", usually before an adjective: 过于紧张. It often sounds negative.

column4: 哈哈，这个笑话太好笑了！
column5: Ha ha, this joke is so funny!
column6: 哈 imitates laughter: 哈哈.

column4: 过海关的时候要检查行李。
column5: When you go through customs, your luggage must be checked.
column6: 海关 is customs at an airport or a border.

column5: His friends are all overseas.
column6: 海外 means abroad, across the sea: 海外朋友 (friends overseas).

column5: I like eating seafood.
column6: 海鲜 is fish, shrimp, crab and shellfish from the sea.

column3: to contain; to hold in the mouth
column5: This drink contains a lot of sugar.
column6: 含 is to have something in it (含糖) or to hold something in your mouth (含着糖).

column4: 这种饮料的糖含量很高。
column5: The sugar content of this drink is very high.
column6: 含量 is how much of something is contained: 水的含量 (the water content).
